subject: Intermittent reachability to FinEdge via hybrid gateway — stale /ghost prefix suspected
messages:
From: Samir Rao <samir@finedge.com>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.com
Cc: edgeops@finedge.com
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent reachability to Redwood via hybrid gateway — observed ghost prefix

Hi Olga,

We're seeing intermittent failures from our payment nodes to Redwood-hosted services over the hybrid gateway. Symptoms: roughly 1-2% of requests fail with TCP RST or timeouts for ~30s, then recover. Trace shows some traffic going to 198.51.100.0/24 — which we do not own — and then blackholing.

We believe this started after a local network change last week but can't find a clear cause. Our ops team captured a pcap and a high-level topology; attaching both.

Can Redwood help verify whether this looks like a stale route advertisement / overlapping prefix coming from your edge, or whether NAT/MTU mismatches on the hybrid gateway could cause the symptoms? This is affecting a subset of API traffic and we have a maintenance window on Tue 18 May if changes are required.

Attachments: packet_capture.pcap (pcap), topology-diagram.svg (svg)

Thanks,
Samir Rao
Site Reliability Manager
FinEdge Payments

Samir — thanks for the note and the attachments. I'm looping in Rishi (network eng) and Marissa (CS) so we can triage. Initial asks to speed diagnosis:

- Confirm whether the affected flows are TLS (443) only, or also internal healthcheck ports (we're seeing both on the pcap).

We'll start with packet timestamps and our edge BGP advertisements. If this looks like a stale prefix on our side we'll treat it as highest priority. If it's a customer-side ghost prefix, we'll propose a short mitigation path for the Tue 18 maintenance window.

Subject: Re: Intermittent reachability to Redwood via hybrid gateway — observed ghost prefix

Quick triage notes after reviewing the pcap and our edge logs: 

1) Evidence of a 'ghost' prefix: I see packets with destination 198.51.100.45 that are getting forwarded to the hybrid gateway, but our edge BGP table has no origin for 198.51.100.0/24. The pcap shows an AS_PATH with an unexpected next-hop injection timestamped 2027-05-14T16:03:40Z — aligns with Samir's timeframe.

2) NAT behavior mismatch: the hybrid gateway is configured to perform SNAT for some customer flows. During the blackhole window we observe ephemeral port reuse leading to collisions for high-throughput sockets (likely due to asymmetric routing when the ghost prefix is present).

3) MTU/fragmentation: I also see repeated TCP MSS clamping to 1400 bytes in some flows, while FinEdge nodes are sending 1500 MTU; fragmentation/reassembly fails intermittently on trunk links which could explain the sudden resets.

Immediate mitigations we can apply (low-risk, quick):
- Add a temporary route policy on the Redwood edge to drop 198.51.100.0/24 and prevent propagation to the hybrid gateway (prevents loops/blackholing).
- Apply a temporary SNAT rule scoped to FinEdge subnets to force symmetric egress mapping during the window.
- Request FinEdge to clamp MTU on their FGW to 1400 to match the observed clamped MSS until routing is stabilized.

If FinEdge can confirm the pcap timeframe and permit the change, we can schedule the edge policy change during Tue 18 maintenance window. I'll attach the extracted pcap segment that demonstrates the AS_PATH injection and the TCP resets.

Attachment: packet_capture.pcap (pcap)

—Rishi

We pulled the FGW config and can see a recent BGP export rule that accidentally redistributes connected summaries; we're evaluating a config change but want to avoid disrupting other peers.

We approve the temporary drop rule on your edge for 198.51.100.0/24 and the scoped SNAT workaround during the maintenance window on Tue 18 May 18:00-18:30 UTC. We will also plan to clamp our FGW MTU to 1400 for the window.

Subject: Escalation summary & cutover plan — FinEdge hybrid gateway ghost prefix

Team — finalizing plan for the Tue 18 maintenance window and documenting escalation summary for records. See timeline and actions below.

Summary: FinEdge inadvertently redistributed a connected summary that created a ghost prefix (198.51.100.0/24) visible to some of our edge peers. When present, traffic from FinEdge to Redwood hit the ghost prefix, caused asymmetric egress via a secondary path, and combined with MTU mismatch led to intermittent TCP resets.

Planned remediation (18 May 18:00-18:30 UTC):
- 18:00: Apply temporary inbound route policy on Redwood edge to drop 198.51.100.0/24 (Rishi) — prevents traffic steering to ghost prefix while FGW config is rolled back.
- 18:05: Apply scoped SNAT on hybrid gateway for FinEdge prefixes (karthik_iyer) — ensures symmetric NAT for high-throughput sockets.
- 18:10: FinEdge performs FGW config rollback to stop redistributing connected summaries (Samir).
- 18:20: FinEdge clamps FGW MTU to 1400 and we monitor for 10 minutes.
- 18:30: If stable, remove temporary drop rule and keep SNAT for 24h while we validate.

Post-mortem owners and follow-ups:
- Rishi: capture control-plane logs and AS_PATH evidence for INF-4892 (JIRA).
- Laura: perform a security group audit to confirm SNAT does not introduce unintended ingress rules.
- Marissa: coordinate customer communications and confirm rollback timeline and post-window validation checklist.

Attachments: packet_capture.pcap (extracted), remediation-playbook.md (KM link will be added to JIRA)
Related links: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/finedge/hybrid-gw-triage-notes, JIRA INF-4892

Please acknowledge — Samir, can you confirm the FGW rollback window and that FinEdge will run the MTU clamp at 18:20 UTC? Laura, flag any security concerns ASAP so we can abort if needed.
